products.overview: High-field NMR usually means liquid helium, quench risk, and a dedicated room. Nanalysis 100 reaches the highest field strength available in a benchtop instrument without any of that. A permanent magnet delivers multinuclear 1D and 2D data at sub-millimolar concentrations, with no cryogen refills and no superconducting magnet to maintain. A touchscreen with onboard processing keeps day-to-day operation straightforward, and low maintenance is a stated design goal, not just a claim. Add the Flow Kit and the same instrument becomes a real-time reaction monitor, demonstrated on a live Wittig reaction. Add the AUTOsample-100 and fifty tubes queue and run automatically, without touching the bench footprint.

faqs.question: What is the Nanalysis 100 – Benchtop NMR Spectrometer used for?
faqs.answer: It's used for multinuclear NMR structure analysis, real-time reaction monitoring, and routine QC, offering the highest field strength available in a benchtop instrument.

faqs.question: Does the Nanalysis 100 require cryogens?
faqs.answer: No. It uses a permanent magnet, eliminating the need for liquid helium refills or cryogen infrastructure entirely.

faqs.question: How do I set up real-time reaction monitoring?
faqs.answer: Add the Flow Kit (NMReady-Flow), which converts the instrument into an online NMR detector, controllable onboard, via NMReady-CONNECT, or through third-party software.

faqs.question: How do I run a large batch of samples unattended?
faqs.answer: Add the AUTOsample-100, which holds 50 tubes across two carousels and runs assigned experiments automatically via onboard queueing software.

faqs.question: What's the difference between the Nanalysis 100 and the 100e?
faqs.answer: The 100e is confirmed as a single-nuclei variant; full comparison detail is confirmed by Inkarp once both are built.

faqs.question: What's the difference between the 100 MHz and 60 MHz models?
faqs.answer: The 60 series (60Pro multinuclear, 60e single-nuclei) offers a lower field strength tier; full comparison detail is confirmed by Inkarp.

faqs.question: What sensitivity can the Nanalysis 100 achieve?
faqs.answer: Sub-millimolar concentrations are confirmed; full detailed sensitivity specifications are confirmed directly by Inkarp.

faqs.question: Can the Flow Kit integrate with other lab equipment?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's confirmed to support integration into a broader laboratory system and can be controlled via third-party software.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Nanalysis 100 – Benchtop NMR Spectrometer in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your base configuration and any AUTOsample-100 or Flow Kit accessories. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

sections.subheading: 100 MHz — the highest field in benchtop NMR. No cryogens, ever.
body: The field strength claim is specific, not vague. 100 MHz, confirmed as the highest available in the benchtop NMR category.
No cryogens changes the whole ownership picture. No liquid helium refills, no quench risk, no dedicated cryogen infrastructure.
Sensitivity reaches sub-millimolar concentrations. Genuinely capable multinuclear 1D/2D work, not just routine single-nucleus checks.
Two accessories extend it in different directions. AUTOsample-100 for unattended batch throughput, the Flow Kit for real-time reaction monitoring.
The Flow Kit's claim has a real demonstrated example. A Wittig reaction monitored live, not just a generic "works for flow chemistry" statement.
This connects to a genuine product family. 100e, 60Pro, and 60e siblings confirmed, spanning both field strength and multinuclear-vs-single-nuclei tiers.

sections.eyebrow: Permanent Magnet Field Strength and Sensitivity
sections.title: Permanent Magnet Field Strength and Sensitivity
body: Benchtop NMR usually trades field strength for convenience. This system is built to reduce that tradeoff rather than accept it.

100 MHz is confirmed as the highest field strength available in the benchtop category, delivered through a permanent magnet rather than a superconducting one, which is what removes cryogens from the picture entirely, no liquid helium refills, no quench risk, no dedicated cooling infrastructure. That field strength supports genuine multinuclear 1D and 2D work at sub-millimolar concentrations, not just routine single-nucleus verification.
